title: Sorting by height
blurb: The reference line: sensors, a diverter and two counters. Sorts tall cartons down a chute and lets short ones pass.

brief.task: Run the belt, feed cartons, and push the tall ones down the chute while the short ones carry on. Two sensors at two heights are all you get: a carton that breaks the high beam is tall, one that breaks only the low beam is short.
brief.uses: panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · conveyor.rotate · emitter.emit · sensor_low.detect · sensor_high.detect · pusher.extend · pusher.extended · pusher.retracted
brief.done: Every tall carton ends up in the chute and every short one at the far end, with counter.tall and counter.short adding up to what you fed. The mushroom stops the line inside 200 ms and Start alone will not restart it.

title: Start / stop station
blurb: A conveyor and an operator panel. Momentary buttons, a latching E-stop, and a lamp that has to reflect the real state.

brief.task: The operator contract, on its own. Start runs the belt, Stop stops it, and the mushroom latches a trip that only Reset clears. Feed a batch of the size the panel's pot asks for and stop when it is made.
brief.uses: panel.start · panel.stop · panel.reset · panel.estop · panel.setpoint · belt.rotate · emitter.emit · part_present.detect · counter.count · produced.value · panel.green · panel.red
brief.done: The batch count reaches the setpoint and the line stops itself. Pressing Start while tripped does nothing; releasing the mushroom does not restart it either. Only Reset then Start brings it back.

title: Tank level control
blurb: Analog end to end. A modulating valve and a level transmitter, with outflow that varies with level — a PID tuned full will overshoot empty.

brief.task: Hold the tank at the level the panel's pot asks for, using the fill and drain valves. Outflow follows Torricelli, so the process gain changes with level: a controller tuned at the top overshoots at the bottom.
brief.uses: panel.setpoint · panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · tank.fill · tank.drain · tank.level · level_readout.value
brief.done: The level settles within a few percent of the setpoint and holds there, and it still settles after you move the pot to a different level. A seized valve (tank.fault) keeps its opening while your command reads zero.

title: Light curtain sorting
blurb: Sorting on a measurement instead of two bits. The curtain reports how tall each carton is, so you choose the threshold in code.

brief.task: Sort on a measurement rather than on two bits. The curtain reports how tall each carton is, in metres, so the threshold is yours to choose — put it on the panel's pot and you can change your mind without editing the program.
brief.uses: panel.setpoint · panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · belt.rotate · emitter.emit · height_gauge.height · height_gauge.blocked · diverter.extend · diverter.extended · diverter.retracted · tall_count.count · short_count.count
brief.done: Cartons above your threshold go down the chute and the rest pass, and moving the pot moves the boundary with no other change. The two counters together equal what the curtain measured.

title: Roller line with weighing
blurb: A roller deck, a checkweigher and an inductive sensor that sees metal only — cardboard passes it as if the lane were empty.

brief.task: Checkweigh. Judge each carton on the peak weight it shows as it crosses the deck, and reject anything over the limit on the panel's pot. The inductive sensor sees metal only, and on this line the steel cartons are also the heavy ones — so two independent instruments should agree.
brief.uses: panel.setpoint · panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · infeed.rotate · scale.rotate · scale.weight · metal_check.detect · emitter.emit · outfeed.count · weight_readout.value · panel.red
brief.done: The cartons you flag over-limit are the same ones the inductive sensor flags as metal. Watch the spacing: two cartons on the deck at once read as one peak, so a real checkweigher line holds the feed while the scale is loaded.

title: Pick & place cell
blurb: A gantry with a vacuum cup, fed by a drive you ramp rather than switch. Three motions to sequence, a scanner that identifies each carton, and a grip that reports whether it actually caught anything.

brief.task: Sequence three motions against feedback, not timers. Ramp the infeed drive, read each carton's code at the scanner, then travel · lower · grip · raise · travel · release to put it on the outfeed. The gantry reports whether the vacuum actually caught anything.
brief.uses: panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · infeed.run · infeed.speed · infeed.actual · scanner.enable · scanner.code · scanner.read · scanner.present · gantry.target · gantry.position · gantry.inposition · gantry.lower · gantry.lowered · gantry.raised · gantry.grip · gantry.holding · outfeed.count
brief.done: Every carton fed reaches the outfeed, and gantry.holding is true on every carry — a cycle that runs with holding false carried air. Careful with inposition: a target written this scan does not reach the machine until the next one, so on the scan that issues a move it still reports the place you are trying to leave.

title: Accumulation buffer
blurb: Cartons pile up behind a blade stop on a belt that never stops, and are let out a batch at a time. The release is timed by encoder pulses, so it stays the same size when you turn the drive up — a timer would not.

brief.task: Let cartons pile up behind the blade stop on a belt that never stops, then release a batch. Time the release by encoder pulses rather than by seconds: the pot is a release window in pulses, which is a distance.
brief.uses: panel.setpoint · panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · buffer.run · buffer.speed · enc.count · enc.reset · stop.raise · stop.up · stop.down · exit_eye.detect · outfeed.rotate · released.count · count_display.value
brief.done: Nothing gets past a raised blade while the belt keeps running, and the same pulse window releases the same amount of product at any drive speed — turn buffer.speed up and the release takes half as long and lets out the same number. A timer would have let out twice as many.

title: Heat treat station
blurb: A thermal process with real inertia: you can heat as fast as the element allows and can only cool at the rate the room takes it. Pure proportional control leaves a standing offset you can measure.

brief.task: Hold the plate at the temperature on the panel's pot. The plant is a first-order lag with a loss to ambient, so holding a temperature needs a standing output — and proportional control can only make one out of a standing error.
brief.uses: panel.setpoint · panel.start · panel.stop · panel.estop · oven.heater · oven.temperature · oven.attemp · temp_gauge.value · temp_readout.value · alarm.beacon · alarm.horn
brief.done: With proportional gain alone the plate parks visibly short of setpoint — measure that offset. Add integral action and it closes. Then fail the element (oven.fault) and watch oven.heater keep reading what you commanded while the temperature falls: the output tells you nothing, only the measurement does.
